      "unit_attributes": {
        "modality_explanation": null,
        "statement": "When the approximate timing of the need for leave is not foreseeable, an employee must provide notice to the employer as soon as practicable under the facts and circumstances of the particular case.",

        "modality_explanation": "The text uses 'generally should be practicable' indicating a qualified recommendation/standard expectation rather than an absolute mandate.",
        "statement": "It generally should be practicable for the employee to provide notice of leave that is unforeseeable within the time prescribed by the employer's usual and customary notice requirements applicable to such leave (see § 825.303(c)).",
        "kind": "recommendation",
        "modality": "should",

    {
      "unit": "F001",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "modality_explanation": null,
        "statement": "Notice may be given by the employee's spokesperson (e.g., spouse, adult family member, or other responsible party) if the employee is unable to do so personally.",
        "kind": "permission",
        "modality": "may",
        "scope_text": "If the employee is unable to provide notice personally",
        "scope_quotes": ["F001"],

        "choice_quote": null,
        "alternative_quotes": null,

    {
      "unit": "F001",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "modality_explanation": null,
        "statement": "If an employee's child has a severe asthma attack and the employee takes the child to the emergency room, the employee is not required to leave his or her child in order to report the absence while the child is receiving emergency treatment.",
        "kind": "exemption",
        "modality": "not_required",
        "scope_text": "If an employee's child has a severe asthma attack and the employee takes the child to the emergency room, while the child is receiving emergency treatment",
        "scope_quotes": ["F001"],
        "context_quotes": null,
        "modality_quote": "would not be required",
        "choice_text": null,
        "choice_quote": null,
        "alternative_quotes": null,
        "logic_quote": null,
        "references": null
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F001",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "modality_explanation": "The text states the employee 'would be expected to call', establishing an expectation/recommendation under the specified condition.",
        "statement": "If the child's asthma attack required only the use of an inhaler at home followed by a period of rest, the employee is expected to call the employer promptly after ensuring the child has used the inhaler.",
        "kind": "recommendation",
        "modality": "should",
        "scope_text": "If the child's asthma attack required only the use of an inhaler at home followed by a period of rest",
        "scope_quotes": ["F001"],

    },
    {
      "unit": "F002",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "modality_explanation": null,
        "statement": "An employee must provide sufficient information for an employer to reasonably determine whether the FMLA may apply to the leave request.",
        "kind": "requirement",
        "modality": "must",
        "scope_text": null,
        "scope_quotes": null,

      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F002",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "modality_explanation": "The passage describes types of information that 'may include' depending on the situation; this denotes descriptive factual possibilities.",
        "statement": "Depending on the situation, the information provided by the employee to determine whether the FMLA applies may include: that a condition renders the employee unable to perform the functions of the job; that the employee is pregnant or has been hospitalized overnight; whether the employee or the employee's family member is under the continuing care of a health care provider; if the leave is due to a qualifying exigency, that a military member is on covered active duty or call to covered active duty status (or has been notified of an impending call or order to covered active duty), that the requested leave is for one of the reasons listed in § 825.126(b), and the anticipated duration of the absence; or if the leave is for a family member that the condition renders the family member unable to perform daily activities or that the family member is a covered servicemember with a serious injury or illness; and the anticipated duration of the absence, if known.",
        "kind": "statement",
        "modality": "possible",
        "scope_text": "Depending on the situation",
        "scope_quotes": ["F002"],
        "context_quotes": null,
        "modality_quote": "may include",

        "choice_quote": null,

    {

      "unit_attributes": {
        "modality_explanation": null,
        "statement": "When an employee seeks leave for the first time for a FMLA-qualifying reason, the employee is not required to expressly assert rights under the FMLA or even mention the FMLA.",
        "kind": "exemption",
        "modality": "not_required",
        "scope_text": "When an employee seeks leave for the first time for a FMLA-qualifying reason",
        "scope_quotes": ["F002"],

      "unit_attributes": {

        "kind": "requirement",
        "modality": "must",
        "scope_text": "When an employee seeks leave due to a qualifying reason, for which the employer has previously provided the employee FMLA-protected leave",
        "scope_quotes": ["F002"],

        "kind": "recommendation",
        "modality": "should",
        "scope_text": null,

        "modality": "must",

        "statement": "Failure to respond to reasonable employer inquiries regarding the leave request may result in denial of FMLA protection if the employer is unable to determine whether the leave is FMLA-qualifying.",
        "kind": "statement",
        "modality": "possible",

unit_attributes.statement: When the approximate timing of the need for leave is not foreseeable, an employee must provide notice to the employer as soon as practicable under the facts and circumstances of the particular case.
unit_attributes.scope_text: When the approximate timing of the need for leave is not foreseeable

unit_attributes.modality_explanation: The text uses 'generally should be practicable' indicating a qualified recommendation/standard expectation rather than an absolute mandate.
unit_attributes.statement: It generally should be practicable for the employee to provide notice of leave that is unforeseeable within the time prescribed by the employer's usual and customary notice requirements applicable to such leave (see § 825.303(c)).
unit_attributes.scope_text: Applicable to leave that is unforeseeable

unit_attributes.statement: Notice may be given by the employee's spokesperson (e.g., spouse, adult family member, or other responsible party) if the employee is unable to do so personally.
unit_attributes.scope_text: If the employee is unable to provide notice personally

unit_attributes.statement: If an employee's child has a severe asthma attack and the employee takes the child to the emergency room, the employee is not required to leave his or her child in order to report the absence while the child is receiving emergency treatment.
unit_attributes.scope_text: If an employee's child has a severe asthma attack and the employee takes the child to the emergency room, while the child is receiving emergency treatment

unit_attributes.modality_explanation: The text states the employee 'would be expected to call', establishing an expectation/recommendation under the specified condition.
unit_attributes.statement: If the child's asthma attack required only the use of an inhaler at home followed by a period of rest, the employee is expected to call the employer promptly after ensuring the child has used the inhaler.
unit_attributes.scope_text: If the child's asthma attack required only the use of an inhaler at home followed by a period of rest

unit_attributes.statement: An employee must provide sufficient information for an employer to reasonably determine whether the FMLA may apply to the leave request.

unit_attributes.modality_explanation: The passage describes types of information that 'may include' depending on the situation; this denotes descriptive factual possibilities.
unit_attributes.statement: Depending on the situation, the information provided by the employee to determine whether the FMLA applies may include: that a condition renders the employee unable to perform the functions of the job; that the employee is pregnant or has been hospitalized overnight; whether the employee or the employee's family member is under the continuing care of a health care provider; if the leave is due to a qualifying exigency, that a military member is on covered active duty or call to covered active duty status (or has been notified of an impending call or order to covered active duty), that the requested leave is for one of the reasons listed in § 825.126(b), and the anticipated duration of the absence; or if the leave is for a family member that the condition renders the family member unable to perform daily activities or that the family member is a covered servicemember with a serious injury or illness; and the anticipated duration of the absence, if known.
When an employee seeks leave for the first time for a FMLA-qualifying reason, the employee is not required to expressly assert rights under the FMLA or even mention the FMLA.
unit_attributes.scope_text: When an employee seeks leave for the first time for a FMLA-qualifying reason

unit_attributes.statement: When an employee seeks leave due to a qualifying reason for which the employer has previously provided the employee FMLA-protected leave, the employee must specifically reference either the qualifying reason for leave or the need for FMLA leave.
unit_attributes.scope_text: When an employee seeks leave due to a qualifying reason, for which the employer has previously provided the employee FMLA-protected leave

unit_attributes.modality_explanation: The text states a definite rule/factual result: calling in sick without more info will not be considered sufficient notice.
unit_attributes.statement: Calling in “sick” without providing more information will not be considered sufficient notice to trigger an employer's obligations under the Act.

unit_attributes.modality_explanation: The text specifies that the employer 'will be expected to obtain', which expresses an administrative expectation/recommendation.
unit_attributes.statement: The employer is expected to obtain any additional required information through informal means.

unit_attributes.modality_explanation: The text explicitly states the employee 'has an obligation to respond', denoting a mandatory duty.
unit_attributes.statement: An employee has an obligation to respond to an employer's questions designed to determine whether an absence is potentially FMLA-qualifying.

unit_attributes.modality_explanation: The source states failure to respond 'may result in denial', expressing a conditional possibility of adverse action.
unit_attributes.statement: Failure to respond to reasonable employer inquiries regarding the leave request may result in denial of FMLA protection if the employer is unable to determine whether the leave is FMLA-qualifying.
unit_attributes.scope_text: If the employer is unable to determine whether the leave is FMLA-qualifying following failure to respond to reasonable inquiries

unit_attributes.statement: When the need for leave is not foreseeable, an employee must comply with the employer's usual and customary notice and procedural requirements for requesting leave, absent unusual circumstances.
unit_attributes.scope_text: When the need for leave is not foreseeable, absent unusual circumstances

unit_attributes.statement: An employer may require employees to call a designated number or a specific individual to request leave.

If an employee requires emergency medical treatment, he or she is not required to follow the call-in procedure until his or her condition is stabilized and he or she has access to, and is able to use, a phone.
unit_attributes.scope_text: If an employee requires emergency medical treatment, until his or her condition is stabilized and he or she has access to, and is able to use, a phone

unit_attributes.modality_explanation: The phrase 'may not be required' explicitly specifies that the requirement might not apply or is not required under the circumstances.
unit_attributes.statement: In the case of an emergency requiring leave because of a FMLA-qualifying reason, written advance notice pursuant to an employer's internal rules and procedures may not be required when FMLA leave is involved.
unit_attributes.scope_text: In the case of an emergency requiring leave because of a FMLA-qualifying reason when FMLA leave is involved

unit_attributes.modality_explanation: The phrase 'may be delayed or denied' indicates a possible consequence rather than an obligation or strict entitlement.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employee does not comply with the employer's usual notice and procedural requirements, and no unusual circumstances justify the failure to comply, FMLA-protected leave may be delayed or denied.
unit_attributes.scope_text: If an employee does not comply with the employer's usual notice and procedural requirements, and no unusual circumstances justify the failure to comply
